corrections.dataSource: World Bank PIP API (pip-grp deciles + median, consumption aggregate)

notes: ST: World Bank PIP national consumption distribution (IOF 2017, gini 0.4073, mean $248/mo PPP) used to rebuild percentiles.
Method: decile means = decile share x mean x 10 (PPP $/person/day), converted x30.44 to monthly; p50 = PIP reported median; p10/p25/p75/p90 linearly interpolated between decile midpoints.
Old entry claimed WID.world 2023 but understated the lower half badly (e.g. p10 30 vs PIP-derived 80); upper tail was roughly right.

PIP welfare type for this country is household consumption per capita - applied to income/posttax/consumption blocks; pretax and labor_income scaled by the entry's own prior block ratios (x1.046, x0.80) to keep internal structure.
wealth block left unchanged - no free wealth-distribution source for this country.
dataYear corrected to PIP survey reporting year 2017.

corrections.dataSource: Derived from US anchor distribution - territory has no permanent resident population

notes: UM (US Minor Outlying Islands) has no permanent population (~0 residents; only transient military/contractor and FWS staff) - DB population 0 set in first pass is correct.
No income survey exists or can exist for a zero-population territory; keeping the US anchor distribution (income block identical to US entry) is the defensible choice per brief.
Original dataSource 'REST Countries & World Bank API 2024' was the known placeholder template string - replaced with an honest derivation label.
costOfLivingIndex 100 (= US baseline) retained: any actual costs incurred there are US-military/import priced.

corrections.dataSource: US Census Bureau 2020 Island Areas Census (income year 2019); shape from US anchor

notes: VI (USVI): previous income block was byte-identical to the PR template copy (p50 1742). Rebuilt from real Census data.

2020 Island Areas Census (income year 2019): per capita income $26,897/yr -> p50 = $2,241/mo nominal USD; median household income $40,408; mean household $57,599; poverty rate 22.8% (census.gov press releases CB22-CN.22 / CB23-CN.18 / CB24-CN.08).
Consistency check: mean household income / avg household size (57,599 / 2.14 = 26,916) matches the published per-capita figure.

Non-median percentiles follow the verified US anchor shape (p10/p50 0.324, p25/p50 0.595, p75/p50 1.568, p90/p50 2.351); p10 additionally x0.85 because USVI poverty rate (22.8%) is roughly double the US rate, implying a fatter lower tail.
Values are nominal USD (VI uses USD); price-level difference is carried separately by costOfLivingIndex 77.
pretax/consumption/labor_income blocks scaled by the entry's own prior block ratios (x1.057/x0.812/x0.800); wealth block left unchanged (no free source).
dataYear set to 2020 census year (income reference year 2019) - Island Areas income data is collected once per decade, no newer source exists.
